definition: The anterior root is the front spinal nerve root that contains efferent motor fibers carrying signals outward from the spinal cord to muscles. In this source, these fibers can be activated during transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation along with posterior sensory root fibers under some conditions.

reasons: The definition claims the anterior root “contains efferent motor fibers carrying signals outward from the spinal cord to muscles,” but the provided packet text does not explicitly support this anatomical description of anterior root contents or direction to muscles.

Although the packet does support that “efferent anterior root fibers can be co-activated” during transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation and that this involves posterior sensory (afferent) root fibers under some circumstances, that support does not validate the unsupported anatomical wording in the first part of the definition.

The packet supports that anterior root fibers are efferent motor fibers and that they can be co-activated during transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation, but it does not support the anatomical gloss ‘the front spinal nerve root.’
‘carrying signals outward from the spinal cord to muscles’ is not stated in the packet and goes beyond the supplied source text.
The second sentence generalizes from a specific study context to a broad definitional claim; the packet only reports an observation under certain circumstances, not a general property of the term.
